findings.title: Chat switch stops every in-progress sign-in watcher
findings.problem: The effect cleanup calls chatGenerationStore.stopAllPromptAuthWatchers() on every contextKey change and on unmount, and signInWatcherStops is module-wide rather than chat-scoped. Success and early-close callbacks resolve rows through getCurrentChatById, which returns only the chat currently on screen, and with the opener cut there is no postMessage or late-callback path any more. The listener's contextKey design (a switch away never ends a flow) therefore no longer holds: the left chat's row stays authenticating with no watcher, and on return the listener re-tracks it and rolls it back to the hint after the hint timeout even if the sign-in already completed.
findings.impact: Switching chats during a sign-in (which the ticket's compliance/MFA case can make long) loses completion detection; the user has to re-run the sign-in. Path is live: contextKey changes on every chat switch.
findings.recommendation: Do not end other chats' watchers on switch. Either stop only the watchers of the chat being left when its rows are gone, or record watcher outcomes against the owning chat by id (not only the current chat), or re-check /status for authenticating rows when a chat becomes current. Add a store or hook test for switch-away-and-back.

findings.title: Chat hint expiry stops the sign-in watcher
findings.problem: useChatAuthCallbacks routes onTimeout (the 60 s hint, admin-configurable) to rollbackPromptAuthRow, which calls stopSignInWatcher(authConfigId) before updating the row. useMCPAuthPrompt does not stop its watcher on the hint and keeps polling to the 600 s cap. With the opener cut, no postMessage can arrive after the hint, so in chat the only completion channel is gone at 60 s. The existing test 'stops the watcher on error' and the hint-expiry re-run test both go through this same method.
findings.impact: A sign-in that takes longer than the hint in chat, which is the device-compliance/MFA scenario this ticket targets and also any reopened 'Open sign-in in a new tab' flow, is never detected; the row stays on the hint message until the user retries. Acceptance criterion AC1 is partial.
findings.recommendation: Stop the watcher only on real error/cancel/early-close paths. Make the hint path update the row without calling stopSignInWatcher (a separate store method or a flag on rollbackPromptAuthRow), and add a test that the watcher survives the hint and still marks success afterwards.

findings.title: Side-effecting helpers placed in the Utils layer
findings.problem: architecture/architecture.md:49 defines Utils as pure functions, data transforms and URL builders, and :63 forbids Utils to mutate global state or trigger side effects. openSignInWindow() calls window.open and assigns window.opener and location.href; watchSignInWindow() (watchSignInWindow.ts:38) starts a setInterval, polls the backend, fires the diagnostics beacon and calls consumer callbacks, and imports reportCallbackDiagnostics from the hook module @/hooks/useAuthCallbackListener. Some existing utils (for example toaster.ts) also have side effects, so the rule is unevenly followed.
findings.impact: The documented layer boundary is crossed, so reviewers and later changes cannot rely on utils being safe to call anywhere, and a util now depends on a React hook module.
findings.recommendation: Move the window-opening and watching behaviour to a layer the guide allows side effects in (store or a feature-scoped module) and keep only the pure isHttpUrl check in src/utils, or record the exception in architecture.md so the guide matches the code.

findings.title: Early-close verdict rests on one status fetch
findings.problem: When window.closed reads true, handleWindowClosed stops the tick and runs a single checkStatus; isAuthenticated maps every fetch failure to false. One transient failure (network, 5xx, refresh) is therefore reported through onClosedEarly ('closed before authentication finished'), the watcher stops, and a misleading window_closed_before_callback beacon is sent. The same outcome follows if an IdP page sets COOP and the browser reports closed=true for a still-open cross-origin window. The callback page now closes itself on success, so a closed window is the normal success path and this check sits on the happy path.
findings.impact: A completed sign-in can be shown as a failure, with the row leaving the live set so a later completion is not detected; recovery needs a re-run. Reachability of the COOP variant against the EPAM IdP was not confirmed, so severity is capped at major.
findings.recommendation: Retry the final status check 2-3 times with short backoff before calling onClosedEarly, and treat a fetch error differently from an explicit non-authenticated status (keep polling for a short grace period). Add a watchSignInWindow test with one failed and one successful final fetch.

findings.title: IdP error codes cannot reach the UI with the opener cut
findings.problem: The callback page's error branch posts status:'error' with the IdP code only when window.opener exists; windows opened through openSignInWindow always have opener=null, so the branch only sends diagnostics. watchSignInWindow reads only status==='authenticated' and window.closed and never an error, so useMCPAuthPrompt.onError and rollbackPromptAuthRow(errorCode) are unreachable for these windows. The tests call those handlers directly and never drive a cut-opener error.
findings.impact: A user who denies consent or hits an IdP error keeps the spinner until the hint, or after closing the tab sees the generic 'device compliance check' text instead of the real error code the old postMessage path showed. Closing the gap needs backend surface (an error context on /status) that the spec lists as a non-goal, so intent must decide.
findings.recommendation: Decide between (a) accepting the generic hint/early-close wording for IdP errors and documenting it, or (b) exposing the callback error code through /status and having watchSignInWindow call onError with it. Add a test for the chosen behaviour.

findings.title: Every successful sign-in now logs WARNING
findings.problem: The callback script's intentional no-opener success branch calls sendDiagnostics with opener_present: !!window.opener, which is false, and result 'success'. build_oauth2_callback_diagnostics_response logs at WARNING whenever opener_present is False, although its docstring says clean successes log at INFO; test_callback_diagnostics_warns_on_lost_opener_and_returns_204 still pins success plus False as a warning.
findings.impact: Each MCP sign-in through the new UI emits a WARNING 'opener_present=False', which drowns the real lost-opener signal and the early-close warnings (AC5) the ticket wants to be findable in backend logs.
findings.recommendation: Have the intentional no-opener success beacon omit opener_present or send null (the check is `is False`), or otherwise mark it, so success without an opener logs at INFO and warnings stay for errors, postMessage failures and real lost openers. Add a test for the intentional no-opener success.
